newsitem.title: UK: Sphere Drake cuts London insurance operations.
newsitem.headline: Sphere Drake cuts London insurance operations.

text.p: Bermuda-based insurer Sphere Drake has stopped writing marine insurance in the London market and may cut up to 150 UK staff supporting its London operations over the course of next year, sources close to the company said.
Sphere Drake's decision to exit the hull and cargo business reflects how difficult it has become to underwrite profitably amid a decline in marine insurance rates, the sources said.

This decision is part of a wider restructuring within the group costing $15 million and which is designed to improve financial performance, customer focus and stability. Some of the marine lines of business had not been making a profit.
"This major restructuring marks the conclusion of a comprehensive strategic review," said chief executive Michael Watson in a statement issued earlier in New York.
"Our review revealed a diverse portfolio with uneven financial performance, but showed excellent financial results from our reinsurance lines over a sustained period," he said.
The immediate impact of the review was the departure of 12 London market underwriters. Over the course of next year, the company may cut up to 150 of its 420 UK staff.
Sphere Drake will also sell its Liverpool-based yacht and cargo underwriting agency Groves, John and Westrup, and is in talks to dispose of its protection and indemnity business.
It will focus on developing its more successful reinsurance businesses and pursue UK and European property insurance lines.
